cards.details: The Government of India Act 1919 provided that a statutory commission would review the constitutional reforms after ten years.
The British Government appointed the Indian Statutory Commission under Sir John Simon, two years ahead of schedule.
The Commission arrived in India and was met with nationwide protests under the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.
Lala Lajpat Rai died due to injuries sustained during a police lathi charge while protesting against the Commission in Lahore.
The Commission submitted its report recommending constitutional reforms and provincial autonomy.
Several recommendations of the Simon Commission influenced the Government of India Act 1935.

items.question: Why was the Simon Commission appointed before the scheduled date?
items.answer: The Conservative Government in Britain appointed it in 1927, two years ahead of schedule, anticipating a possible change in government.

items.question: Who was the chairman of the Simon Commission?
items.answer: Sir John Simon, a prominent British politician and lawyer.

items.question: Why did Indians boycott the Simon Commission?
items.answer: Because the Commission contained no Indian member despite being tasked with reviewing India's constitutional future.

items.question: What famous slogan became associated with the Commission?
items.answer: 'Simon Go Back', which became the symbol of nationwide protests.

items.question: Which nationalist leader died after injuries suffered during anti-Simon protests?
items.answer: Lala Lajpat Rai, who was injured in a police lathi charge in Lahore.

traps.title: UPSC Civil Services Common Traps
items: Trap 1: Confusing the Simon Commission (1927) with the Nehru Report (1928). The former was a British-appointed commission; the latter was an Indian constitutional proposal.
Trap 2: Assuming the Commission recommended immediate dominion status. It did not.
Trap 3: Believing Indians opposed the recommendations alone. The primary objection was the absence of Indian representation.
Trap 4: Confusing the Simon Commission with the Round Table Conferences. The Commission preceded and influenced the Conferences.

sections.title: 1. Background and Appointment
sections.content:
The Simon Commission, officially known as the Indian Statutory Commission, was appointed by the British Government in November 1927 under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon.

Constitutional Background
  • Government of India Act 1919: Promised a review of constitutional reforms after ten years.
  • Early Appointment: The Commission was appointed in 1927 instead of 1929.
  • Political Context: British authorities sought to evaluate the working of dyarchy and propose future reforms.
Composition
  • Chairman: Sir John Simon.
  • Seven Members: All members were British parliamentarians.
  • No Indian Representation: This became the main reason for widespread opposition.

sections.title: 2. Indian Response and Nationwide Protests
sections.content:
The Simon Commission triggered one of the largest united political protests during the freedom struggle.

Political Opposition
  • Congress Boycott: The Indian National Congress rejected the Commission.
  • Muslim League: Major factions also opposed it.
  • National Unity: Several political organizations joined the boycott movement.
Protest Movement
  • Slogan: 'Simon Go Back' echoed throughout India.
  • Black Flag Demonstrations: Protesters greeted Commission members with black flags.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai: Led the Lahore protest and later succumbed to injuries from police action.

sections.title: 3. Recommendations and Constitutional Significance
sections.content:
The Simon Commission submitted its report in 1930 and proposed several constitutional reforms.

Major Recommendations
  • Abolition of Dyarchy: Recommended ending dyarchy in provinces.
  • Provincial Autonomy: Proposed greater self-government in provinces.
  • Federal Structure: Suggested a future federation involving provinces and princely states.
  • Franchise Expansion: Recommended increasing voter participation.
Historical Impact
  • Nehru Report 1928: Encouraged Indians to draft their own constitutional framework.
  • Round Table Conferences: Influenced subsequent constitutional discussions.
  • Government of India Act 1935: Several recommendations were incorporated into this landmark legislation.
  • Freedom Struggle: Strengthened nationalist unity and intensified demands for self-government.
